text:
jessica_support: Customer reporting 403 on iOS and says there is no visible request id in the app UI. They can reproduce consistently when hitting /v1/generate. Asking what exact artifacts we need and how to get them from a non-dev user.
customer_john: I can reproduce, I9m not on a Mac. App shows a red error screen with code 403, no extra info. What9s the easiest thing I can send?
jessica_support: Short answer: a sysdiagnose bundle (if you can grab it), an app-level network capture (HAR from webview or a Charles/Proxyman export), plus a minimal curl repro with headers if possible. If non-dev, we can guide through TestFlight logs or an in-app "Save logs".
mobile_sean: Steps for iOS non-dev: 1) Reproduce the error 2) Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Analytics & Improvements -> Share iPhone Analytics -> create sysdiagnose via holding Volume Up+Down+Power? (note: exact key combo varies) 3) If they can connect to a Mac, use Xcode9s Devices window to download sysdiagnose. If not, ask them to upload the analytics file from Settings -> Analytics -> Shareable logs.
devops_jamie: For webviews: ask customer to enable remote debugging (if it9s WKWebView -> Safari Develop menu) and export a HAR. If they use an embedded native SDK call (not web), request the SDK debug bundle: open app dev menu -> toggle verbose logs -> reproduce -> use in-app "Export logs".
eng_oncall_lee: Important: we need any headers that traveled with the failing call. Look for Authorization, x-request-id / request-id / x-rw-session / x-session-hash and any proxy traces (via Via or X-Forwarded-For). Also capture timestamps around the failure (local timezone + epoch) so we can correlate with our traces.
cust_john: I9m not technical enough for Xcode or Charles. What9s the one click method?
jessica_support: If they9re on TestFlight: open TestFlight app -> select build -> tap "Send Beta Feedback" -> attach screenshot and include phrase "include logs". That sends a sysdiagnose equivalent to us. Otherwise ask them to: Settings -> Privacy -> Analytics & Improvements -> Analytics Data -> find the latest sysdiagnose entry -> Share -> email to support@example.com (we9ll accept the file).
mobile_sean: When they share the bundle, tell them to rename the file to include the failing timestamp and their user id (e.g., john_2024-11-05_14-22_sysdiagnose.tar.gz). That speeds up lookup.
devops_jamie: If they can do a network capture, here9s a minimal curl template to reproduce from a Mac/Linux shell. Replace placeholders with their token and the captured path: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \\n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n -H "X-Request-Id: <from-capture>" \\n -d '{"input":"short prompt to reproduce"}' \\n 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
```
eng_oncall_lee: If they can9t provide X-Request-Id, we can still search by time + client IP + user id. Include the exact ISO timestamp (eg 2024-11-05T14:22:36-07:00) and the app's reported client IP from Settings -> About -> Network (if shown).
jessica_support: Quick grep commands we use after they upload sysdiagnose (share with us): 
```
# list tar contents and search for request id strings
tar -tzf sysdiagnose-*.tar.gz | grep -iE "request|reqid|session|har|network"
# extract then search logs inside bundle
mkdir /tmp/sd && tar -xzf sysdiagnose-*.tar.gz -C /tmp/sd
grep -R --line-number -i "x-request-id\|request-id\|x-session\|trace" /tmp/sd || true
```
Note: sometimes mobile obfuscates header names; also search for URL paths '/v1/generate' or '/v1/embeddings'.
customer_john: I found a small file called log-2024-11-05.txt in the bundle. Do I paste it here?
jessica_support: Please upload to the ticket or paste as an attachment (not inline if big). If small, paste snippet and include the exact failing line. We9ll look for lines that show a 403 and any request tokens.
mobile_sean: If the customer can open a terminal, ask them to run this to extract potential req ids quickly: ```
# from the extracted sysdiagnose folder
grep -oE "[a-f0-9]{8}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{4}-[a-f0-9]{12}" -R /tmp/sd | head -n 20
```
This looks for UUID-like request ids we commonly emit.
devops_jamie: Also ask them to include the SDK version from About -> App Info and whether they9re on cellular vs wifi. Proxy middleboxes often strip or rewrite headers.
eng_oncall_lee: If we can't find any id in their bundle, we escalate to a server-side search: provide us with app user id, approximate time window (start/end), and client IP. We9ll correlate with ingress logs and return candidate request ids.
jessica_support: TL;DR checklist to send to customer: 1) one sysdiagnose or TestFlight feedback with logs 2) HAR or proxy export if possible 3) a minimal curl with headers (replace token) if they can run it 4) exact ISO timestamp(s) of failure 5) SDK version and client IP 6) indicate if they use proxy/VPN.
cust_john: Ok I9ll try TestFlight feedback and attach the log file. Thanks.
deploy-bot: Automated note: if a matching request id is later found in prod traces, this thread will be updated with trace link. :gear:
